input.text: Welcome to the Summer Palace — the greatest imperial garden that survives on Earth, and Beijing's masterpiece of water and hills. Covering nearly three square kilometers — three-quarters of it water — this was the summer retreat of the Qing court, who fled the heat of the Forbidden City for the breezes of Kunming Lake. Everything here is deliberate: the lake was expanded by hand, and the earth dug from it was piled into Longevity Hill before you. Walk the Long Corridor — seven hundred meters of painted walkway, its beams holding thousands of classical scenes — said to be the longest painted corridor in the world. At its end, the Marble Boat waits: a stone vessel where the Empress Dowager Cixi famously lounged — paid for, critics said, with money meant for the imperial navy. And the story ended as critics warned. Come at golden hour, rent a boat, and see what emperors saw.
